_comment: Standards row: names, one-line roles and a plain status; no third-party logos we do not have rights to use. Checked against the code on 2026-09-25, 2026-09-26 and 2026-09-30. A passport is signed as a JSON Web Signature (RFC 7515) under a did:web identity. W3C Verifiable Credentials are the access credentials readers present, NOT the passport's own format; the node verifies them and checks a W3C Bitstring Status List when a credential names one (fail-closed: an unreachable list counts as revoked), but the credentials it issues itself carry no status list and simply expire (dpp-engine handlers/credentials.rs, 'Revocation is expiry'). The SD-JWT VC form of a passport is in the open library but the node does not issue it yet. The AAS export follows the structure but uses Odal's own identifiers (urn:odal-node:), hence 'Partly in place'. The sixth is the set of six harmonised DPP standards cited by Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736 (OJ 15.7.2026: EN 18216, 18219, 18220, 18221, 18222, 18223; not a range, there is no 18217 or 18218); alignment is work in progress, and the row links to the docs page that sets out, standard by standard, where the software stands. Status values: 'In place' or 'Partly in place' only; say which in plain words, never 'conformant'.
